summary: This chunk adds four new files from an eval run of an adversarial on-call-plan review. user_notes.md documents workarounds (charter filled without a live user, outputs redirected to with_skill/outputs/, report.md written via shell heredoc after a harness guard rejected Write, retest stage deliberately left pending). grading.json records six passed expectations (0 failed) about the review report's quality, execution metrics (10 tool calls, 1 error), timing (1203.5s, 62457 tokens), a claims list distinguishing verified factual claims from unverifiable process claims, and eval_feedback suggesting new expectations for severity calibration and fabrication resistance. timing.json (appearing twice, in run-1/ and at the top level) holds the same token/duration totals.

claims.text: A harness guard rejected the Write tool for report.md, so it was written via a shell heredoc instead, counted as the one error in metrics.json
Stage 5 (retest) is pending by design, intended to run cold in a later session
All six expectations passed with a 1.0 pass rate
Execution had 10 total tool calls, 7 steps, and 1 error
Total run took 1203.5 seconds and used 62457 tokens
Twelve raw findings were merged to eight, with none killed
Three fresh-eyes adversaries attacked in parallel
The database failover runbook contains a destructive branch and runbooks hold unstated tribal knowledge
top-level timing.json duplicates run-1/timing.json exactly (62457 tokens, 1203549 ms)

risks.note: Identical timing.json content is written to two separate paths (run-1/ and top-level); redundant duplication rather than a single source of truth.
The claim that 12 findings were merged to 8 with none killed is explicitly marked unverified in the same file because no transcript exists to check it.

Runbook content claims (destructive branch, tribal knowledge) are marked verified:false since the artifact never describes actual runbook contents; the report itself self-flags these as Plausible rather than Confirmed.

least_confident: Whether the harness guard behavior described in user_notes.md (rejecting Write for report.md) reflects a general policy or a one-off condition specific to this run is not something this chunk clarifies.
